added_failures_note: measured from the reviewed run's own armed gate logs; see verified_independently.

findings.text: the production dispatch still disposes every live pointer, so the node's goal is not delivered on the path its own plan measured at 463 s. The read narrows only when a caller supplies candidate_paths, and the sole production caller that does is refuse_widen_scope_conflicts (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1790, reached only from reckon/crew/claims.py:99); crew.dispatch and the plan-review read at reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1059 pass none, so reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:358 sets relevant=True for every pointer and the git cost the section exists to remove is untouched there. The new test cannot see this because it calls the private read directly rather than going through crew.dispatch. Contrast with the manifest, which records only the _WORKTREE_REPOSITORY_FIELDS deviation and describes the read as narrowed. The dispatch.py call site lies outside the node's declared write paths, so this needs the coordinator: either wire the candidate paths in, or record that the section's write paths do not reach the file its deliverable requires.

the fixture gives every claim in a repository the same worktree path (tests/test_a_dispatch_asks_git_only_about_claims_that_could_meet_its_own.py:262 and :269), so assert len(probes) <= 2 measures a cache hit that a real fleet cannot produce: of the 41 live pointers on this workstation today, 37 name a distinct checkout path, and the identity cache is keyed by the checkout path probed, so one probe is still paid per pointer that has its own worktree (about 37 + 6 rather than 6). The fragment's closing claim that "at most one rev-parse per distinct repository" holds is therefore unsupported by this fixture, and would only hold if the deliberately-unapplied field reorder were restored. A fixture giving each claim its own linked worktree would show the real count; the positive-control lesson applies to the count as well as to the check.

assert all(claim.binding or claim.disposition_reason for claim in claims) is documented as proving that "a claim nobody judged would carry neither", but reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:384 sets binding=True if disposition is None, so an unread claim satisfies the disjunction and this assertion cannot redden on the very case its comment names. The sibling assertion on the preceding line (not any(claim.unread)) does carry that guard, so the disjunction is redundant rather than load-bearing, but as written it is an assertion that cannot name a condition under which it fails.

the done_when requires that ruff check and ruff format --check findings on every changed path do not exceed base, but the manifest records logs for the two suite arms and the negative control only, so the ruff half of the gate has no log to read. I ran it: head 8 findings on the changed files against the base arm's 9, and ruff format --check reports all three files already formatted, so the claim holds; it is the record that is missing, and this node's manifest names no log for it.

justifications.durability: the declared negative control at logs/negative-control.log turns the wrapper's disposition count from 2 to 42 and reddens two of the new tests, so the narrowing is genuinely guarded, but reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:384 defaults binding=True on an unread claim, which makes the assertion at tests/test_a_dispatch_asks_git_only_about_claims_that_could_meet_its_own.py:373 unable to redden on the case its comment names.
justifications.evidence: the gate at logs/head-arm.log and logs/base-arm.log records its revisions, its literal command and its EXIT= line, but the done_when's "at most one rev-parse per distinct repository" bound rests on a fixture that gives every claim in a repository one shared checkout path (tests/test_a_dispatch_asks_git_only_about_claims_that_could_meet_its_own.py:262).
justifications.fit: the new names (unread, candidate_paths, identity_cache, _resolve_repository_identity) name mechanism rather than plan items and the module docstring at reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:308 follows the surrounding idiom.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1378 calls _repository_scope_claims() with no candidate_paths, so candidates is None at reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:358 and every live pointer's disposition is still read on the dispatch path the plan's 463 s measurement names.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/dispatch_sections.py:69 already owns a per-spelling memo of repository_identity with a result-aliasing step; the change adds a second, read-scoped memo parameter to the same owner: the same capability, twice, with the older one left unextended.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 7cb177e8a..0be6a3dc0 touches only the four declared write paths, with no incidental reformatting and nothing under docs/figures/.

notes: Independent review of the reviewed run at head 0be6a3dc0 against base 7cb177e8a. The landed read is correct in itself: narrowing by candidate paths cannot drop a collision because relevance uses the same containment rule the arbitration does, the negative control raises the disposition count from 2 to 42 and reddens two tests, the arms add no failure, and the field-order deviation is real and recorded. The blocking finding is that the production dispatch passes no candidate paths, so the plan's central benefit is not delivered on the path it names; the node could not fix that inside its write paths.
